function.name: memory_open
function.description: Read persistent memory. No argument returns the index: one line per entry with its name, size in bytes and description. Pick from it and pass every entry you need in one call. Each body comes with numbered lines, the numbers memory_grep reports and memory_move takes. Open the index at the start of a session, and whenever you need context on the user, their projects or the people around them.

names.description: Entries to open, for instance ["areas/qwentts-cpp", "people/allozaur"]. Omit for the index alone.
names.title: Entries to open

function.name: memory_grep
function.description: Search persistent memory. Returns every line that matches the pattern, across all entries, as <name>:<line>: <text>, or <name>:description: <text> for a description. Use it to find where a subject, a name or a reference lives before opening or moving anything.

function.name: memory_write
function.description: Write persistent memory. Name is <group>/<slug>: areas for ongoing projects, people for the ones the user works with, topics for lasting facts about them. old_str and new_str replace a unique string, new_str alone appends, old_str alone removes it along with the line break that follows it. new_str takes as many lines as you have to write. Pass description whenever the edit changes what the entry is about, and when creating one. Store what the user stated, not what you concluded. The index line of the entry comes back with the result.

description.title: One line on what this entry covers, shown in the index

new_str.title: Replacement text, or the lines to append

old_str.title: Text to replace or remove, must appear exactly once in the body

function.name: memory_move
function.description: Move whole lines of an entry, byte for byte, by the numbers memory_open shows. The lines land at the end of the destination, or after the line where after_str ends, and leave the source; the source itself as destination reorders it. The destination must exist, memory_write creates entries. A move never deletes anything. Use it to reorganize memory instead of rewriting text with memory_write.

lines.title: Line numbers of the source, for instance "12-15,22"

to.title: Destination entry name, <group>/<slug>, the source itself to reorder

after_str.title: Unique string of the destination, the lines land after the line where it ends

function.name: memory_drop
function.description: Remove a whole entry from persistent memory, only when the user asks to forget that subject. To remove a single fact, use memory_write with old_str alone.
